variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the container. Count the cubes named in the goal; that is the number of targets N, equal to the length of target_containers. Rule for A (pick up): choose A whenever the gripper is not holding a container (fingers fully open, or gripper raised out of frame) and picks_done is less than N. Point at the container listed at index picks_done in target_containers (the first entry when picks_done is 0, the second when picks_done is 1). Write the point as that container's position with y reduced by about 3 pixels (e.g. container [84, 156] gives point [81, 158]). If the container visible at this step has drifted slightly from the stored position, point at the visible container nearest the stored position. Rule for B (put down): choose B whenever the gripper is holding a container (fingers partly closed, around 40-60% open, gripper raised after a grasp) and picks_done is less than N, meaning another target still has to be picked up. After the put-down the next decision step will show fingers fully open; then apply rule A for the next target. When picks_done equals N and the robot is holding a container, the task is complete and no further decision is expected; if asked anyway, choose B. If a situation matches no rule (e.g. fingers closed on nothing, 0% open, or the memory is inconsistent with the scene), choose A and point at the entry of target_containers at index picks_done, or at the first entry if that index does not exist, and do not change picks_done.

fields.name: target_containers
fields.description: Ordered list of container positions, one per cube named in the goal, in the order the goal names them. At the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown): for each cube color named in the goal, read that cube's position from the demonstration steps before the containers appear, then take the container whose position is within a few pixels of it after the containers appear, and write that container's position; the cubes are no longer listed once containers are shown. Copy the list unchanged at every later step. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of the positions of the containers that the goal asks for, in goal order (first the container hiding the first named cube, then the one hiding the next named cube, if any). Each position is the demonstration position of the container that came down over that cube, i.e. the container whose coordinates lie within a few pixels of where that cube was before the containers appeared. Filled in at the first decision step from the demonstration steps and never changed afterwards. e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]]

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of target containers picked up so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. At any later step, take the carried-in value and add one if the execution steps since the previous decision step show the fingers going from fully open to partly closed (about 40-60% open) with the gripper then raised, i.e. a container was grasped and lifted; otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of target containers the robot has picked up so far in this episode. 0 at the first decision step. Increases by one at the first decision step whose execution steps show the robot having closed its fingers on a container and lifted it (fingers partly closed, around 40-60% open, gripper raised); stays the same at steps that show a put-down or no grasp. e.g. 1

history.critique:
field picks_done, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  DELETE. In every episode the goal names one cube and the episode ends at the first decision step, the moment the robot is commanded to pick up that container. No later decision step exists, so the count is written once as 0 and never read. It breaks NECESSITY: nothing in the goal or the steps ever needs a pick count. Remove the field entirely.

field target_containers, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  KEEP, simplified. Holds the demonstration position of the container that came down over the cube named in the goal: the container whose coordinates lie within a few pixels of where that cube sat before the containers appeared. One entry per cube named in the goal (one in every episode seen), in goal order. Written at the first decision step from the demonstration steps and never changed. It is kept because the demonstration is shown only at the first decision step; should any later decision step occur (the pick not yet achieved), the target can be recovered from nowhere else. e.g. [[92, 87]]

field picks_done, POLICY PROMPT
  DELETE. Do not write this field. The task ends when the container hiding the named cube has been picked up, so there is no count to keep.

field target_containers, POLICY PROMPT
  At the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown): find the cube whose color the goal names in the demonstration steps before the containers appear, then after the containers appear take the container listed within a few pixels of that cube's position, and write that container's position as the single entry. At any later step copy the carried-in list unchanged. e.g. [[92, 87]]

the policy prompt for subgoal
  The rules that counted targets, compared picks_done to N, and chose B (put down) when holding a container are to be removed; no episode ever reaches a put-down, and picks_done no longer exists. The instruction becomes one rule. Rule A (pick up): at the first decision step, when the gripper is raised out of frame with fingers fully open and the memory is empty, identify from the demonstration steps the cube whose color the goal names, take the container that appeared within a few pixels of that cube's position, and choose A pointing at that container with y reduced by about 3 pixels and x unchanged (container [92, 87] gives point [89, 86]). At any later decision step where the gripper is not holding a container (fingers fully open or gripper raised out of frame), choose A again pointing at the first entry of target_containers, adjusted the same way, or at the visible container nearest that stored position if it has drifted. If the gripper is holding a container (fingers partly closed, about 40-60% open, gripper raised), the task is complete; if asked anyway, choose B. Keep the fallback: when a situation matches no rule, choose A at the first entry of target_containers.

applied.refused: Nothing is committed. This round scored 0 wrong subgoals and 0 wrong memories across 5 steps, so no failure needs settling. The report asks to delete picks_done, reduce target_containers to a single entry, and strip the put-down rule and the N-count from the subgoal instruction. That request is drawn from one minibatch in which every goal named one cube and every episode ended at its first decision step. The initializer's minibatch included two-cube goals (the e.g. [[81, 95], [66, 143]] was written from it), where the robot must pick up a first container, put it down, and pick up a second; on those episodes picks_done is read at the second and later decision steps and the B rule is required. Deleting them would undo the initial design to fit one round's episodes and would break NECESSITY and SUFFICIENCY on the next multi-target episode. The existing instructions already handle the single-cube case correctly (N=1, picks_done=0, rule A at index 0), as the perfect score shows, so the simplification buys nothing.
